Class LightProperties

java.lang.Object
net.murat.light.LightProperties
public class LightProperties extends Object
Holds calculated light properties for shading. ZERO-ALLOCATION: Uses pre-allocated temp objects. Compatible with Java 6-8 without lambdas.

THREAD-SAFETY FIX: the original version used `static final` scratch fields (TEMP_DIR, TEMP_POS, TEMP_RESULT) shared by ALL callers across ALL threads. If the ray tracer renders with more than one thread (e.g. tile-based or row-based parallel rendering), two threads calling getLightProperties(...) concurrently would stomp on each other's scratch data, producing flickering / randomly wrong lighting that is very hard to reproduce or debug.

Fix: scratch vectors are now per-thread via ThreadLocal instead of per-class. This keeps the same "zero steady-state allocation" property (each thread allocates its own scratch Vector3 exactly ONCE, on first use, then reuses it forever) while making concurrent calls from different threads safe. Single-threaded callers see no behavioral or performance difference at all; only the multi-threaded case changes (from "silently broken" to "correct").

TEMP_PROPS (a shared LightProperties instance) was removed because it was declared but never actually used anywhere in this class - dead field, not a behavioral change.

      public static final void getLightProperties(Light light, Point3 point, LightProperties target)
      ZERO-ALLOCATION: Gets light properties into the provided target. Thread-safe: TEMP_DIR/TEMP_POS below are now per-thread (see class javadoc), so concurrent calls from different rendering threads no longer corrupt each other's scratch data.
      Parameters:
      light - The light source
      point - The surface point
      target - The LightProperties instance to fill (MUST NOT BE NULL)
